newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI says Gencor merger to dilute EPS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI says Gencor merger to dilute EPS.

text.p: QNI Ltd said on Friday the proposed merger with Gencor Ltd's nickel unit would dilute earnings per share (EPS) by 20 percent in the first year, would be earnings dilutive in the second year, and would be earnings positive in the third and fourth year.
QNI said that Gencor had indicated it would not make a full cash takeover bid for QNI if their merger proposal was rejected by shareholders.
It said the Cerro Matoso nickel mine in Columbia had been valued at between A$1.3 billion and A$1.8 billion.

"They've (Gencor) indicated they are not interested in bidding for the company (if the merger is rejected)," QNI managing director Wyn Davies told an openly hostile briefing for analysts and investors.
"I think it would be a tragedy if we didn't grab this opportunity," Davies said. QNI were sold down sharply on Friday morning as an investor revolt over the merger gathered momentum.

Analysts and brokers have said there is a strong possibility the deal would be rejected at the shareholders meeting needed to approve the deal, because Gencor was seen to have paid too little for its controlling interest in QNI.
Gencor is contributing its nickel division, including its Cerro Matoso nickel operations in Colombia, in exchange for a 56-percent stake in an enlarged QNI vehicle.

Davies told the briefing, under repeated questioning about the mine's valuation, that Cerro Matoso was valued at A$1.3 billion to A$1.8 billion recently by Gencor when the South African miner was considering selling the mine independently.

He said however QNI could not give the valuation it used for Cerro Matoso in its merger considerations, but that one would be provided when the merger was assessed by independent valuers Grant Samuels and Associates.

Also under repeated questioning, a QNI official said the merger would be earnings per share dilutive in the first two years, because of depreciation and amortisation costs, but in the third and fourth years, the merger would be very earnings per share positive.
"It would be about 20 percent in the first year," the official told the briefing when asked how earnings dilutive it would be.
At 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT), QNI shares were 10 cents lower at A$2.55 with almost five million shares traded.
